newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia's ailing Privredna Bank sees big overhaul.
newsitem.headline: Croatia's ailing Privredna Bank sees big overhaul.

text.p: Croatia's ailing Privredna Banka Zagreb (PBZ) said on Monday it hoped to regain a key role in the banking sector after being overhauled by the government.

"...We can very soon have a leading commercial and privatised (bank in) Privredna Banka Zagreb, which will spur overall development within the country borders and act as a key financial agent in international operations," PBZ's outgoing president Martin Katicic said in a statement.
On December 17, Katicic was replaced by Ivan Tesija, chief of supervision at the central bank, who will manage and represent PBZ during the rehabilitation process.
Katicic said he was confident the decision to overhaul it would not only resolve mounting problems in PBZ, but also enable its future business on a healthy foundation.
The bank services most utilities and other vital parts of the Croatian economy. But it has been dragged down by liquidity problems and bad debts.
By 1991, PBZ had accumulated some $1.5 billion or 66 percent of the total foreign debt of Croatia, then part of communist Yugoslavia.
These liabilities, some of which mature next year, pose a big problem for the bank as do other loans to ailing state-owned firms and businesses damaged by the 1991-95 conflicts with rebel Serbs.

Its overhaul is planned in two stages during which a government-run bank rehabilitation agency will first clear PBZ's portfolio of debts owed by state companies, including the oil utility INA, railways and others listed for restructuring.
In exchange, the agency will take virtual control of the bank, recapitalise it, reshuffle the management and eventually sell it off.
The cost of the operation is estimated at roughly three billion kuna (some $540 million), for which Croatia expects considerable backing from the World Bank.
The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) is also said to be considering help for to Privredna. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
